investigations.question: After a restart with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a CommitTrackingLogStore, is the node's in-memory configuration still the committed configuration retained in its own log?
investigations.hypothesis: restoreFromCommittedLogs advances lastApplied before the startup configuration scan, so committed LogConfiguration entries at or below the restored commit index are skipped and the node keeps the snapshot (or empty) configuration.
investigations.discriminator: Restart identical stores with the flag on and off and compare configuration index, server count and hasVote immediately after NewRaft returns; then repeat with a snapshot older than a committed configuration change.

latest_interpretation.rationale: The parent question is answered by receipt 75c355f2a4634b5193fa97e4de987fe0 (exit 0, six events, no parse loss) with receipt 3e2dd223dd5f43409c21066a1ca43175 as the earlier execution of the same declaration: with RestoreCommittedLogs on and no snapshot, the restarted node reported after_latest_index 0, after_servers 0 and after_has_vote false while after_commit_index 11 and after_last_applied 11 were restored (violated at witness event index 1 against the admission at index 0 recording before_latest_index 1 with one server), and the flag-off control kept index 1 with one voter (evaluated event index 3). The snapshot-present case in the same receipt shows the loss with a committed membership change newer than the snapshot (violated at witness index 5, admission 4). Mechanism: NewRaft initialises configurations to its zero value, restoreSnapshot (api.go:655-681) is the only persistent-state producer of a configuration and the startup log scan (api.go:604-620) is the only other, but restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs first and advances lastApplied to the persisted commit index, so committed LogConfiguration entries at or below it are skipped; processLogs forwards them to the FSM without ever updating r.configurations (raft.go:1366-1391). The child question has since witnessed the multi-voter variant and its consequences: with a five-voter committed configuration and a three-voter snapshot the restarted node came back at index 1 with three servers (receipt b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826, violated at witness index 15, control 18), and after a heal the two sides held different entries at the same log index (receipt a608e5f60ae4415981c1024522a24a0d, violated at witness index 27, control 29), while the two-second window (receipt 4e9eaa72cf594018b8414a8d8efb7cb3) is a negative for loss of an acknowledged entry.
counterevidence: The flag-off controls keep the committed configuration in every cited execution, isolating the recovery path rather than the restart, the stores or the applied entries.
A snapshot can supply a configuration (api.go:677-678) but only as of its configuration index, which is why the snapshot-present case needed a configuration change newer than the snapshot.
limitations: The parent's own witness uses a single-voter configuration and a nonvoter addition; voter-adding changes, minority leadership and the post-heal log disagreement are witnessed under the child question and are not observed in the parent's own executions.

No lost acknowledged entry is witnessed anywhere in this run: the child's two-second window is a negative for loss and its eight-second window shows the two logs disagreeing at one index rather than an entry disappearing.
The startup-blocking and authority questions are separate and are not part of this account.

Receipts b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826, a608e5f60ae4415981c1024522a24a0d and 4e9eaa72cf594018b8414a8d8efb7cb3 belong to the child multi-voter question (five voters grown from three after a deliberate snapshot, isolation of the restarted node with one committed voter) and are cited here only for the follow-on consequences named in the limitations. investigations.question: Does a restart with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs and a large committed backlog complete, given that restoreFromCommittedLogs calls processLogs before the FSM goroutine is started?
investigations.hypothesis: processLogs pushes one message per MaxAppendEntries-sized batch into fsmMutateCh, whose capacity is 128, while runFSM is only started after NewRaft returns; a backlog requiring more than 128 batches blocks NewRaft forever.
investigations.discriminator: Commit N committed entries with no snapshot and restart: a backlog whose batch count is below the queue capacity returns promptly, while a slightly larger one never returns within a bounded wait.

latest_interpretation.rationale: Receipt 78d56323ae6646da8140c38ebed9bd1c (exit 0, ten events, no parse loss) resolves both comparisons of the corrected declaration. Comparison 0 is violated by witness event index 9: with RestoreCommittedLogs on, no snapshot and 8402 committed entries (commit index 8402, admission event index 8), NewRaft had not returned after the bounded 15 second wait. Comparison 1 holds at evaluated event index 7: the same restart with 8002 committed entries returned in 2 ms, so the two sizes bracket the failure and rule out general replay slowness. Source mechanism: NewRaft creates fsmMutateCh with capacity 128 (api.go:558-561) and starts the FSM, main and snapshot goroutines only after the startup work at api.go:632-639, while restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) calls processLogs, which pushes one message per MaxAppendEntries batch into that queue (raft.go:1296-1320); a replay needing more than 128 batches blocks on an unconsumed channel inside NewRaft with no retry, timeout or fallback in that path. Consequence: the node never finishes starting, so duties that depend on it (elections, replication, convergence) are stalled indefinitely rather than bounded; the boundary near 8192 committed entries with default MaxAppendEntries of 64 and default TrailingLogs of 10240 keeps this inside ordinary settings. The earlier receipt 04fccedbacf54df3b7064fd16fa57b26 already witnessed the violation but could not complete the control because both sizes shared one result event name; it is retained as prior evidence of the same behaviour.

knowledge.assertion: NewRaft blocks forever on an unconsumed fsmMutateCh when the RestoreCommittedLogs replay needs more batches than the queue holds.

counterevidence: The sub-capacity case returns immediately in two independent receipts (0 ms and 2 ms for 8002 entries), so the outcome is not general slowness.
No snapshot existed in either case, so the blocking is independent of snapshot restore.
limitations: The failing case is a bounded wait, not an infinite-run proof; a later repair or a different schedule is not excluded by this observation alone.
The queue capacity of 128 and the batch size of 64 are read from the source, not measured.
The failure was observed with the in-memory commit-tracking store; whether a durable store changes the size boundary is not established.

investigations.question: After that restart, does the node ever regain authority within a bounded window, or does the configuration it failed to rebuild leave it permanently unable to campaign?
investigations.hypothesis: With an empty or snapshot-age configuration, runFollower takes the 'no known peers' branch and the hasVote gate never opens, so the node stays Follower and the single-voter cluster never regains a leader.
investigations.discriminator: Restart the same single-node state with the flag on and off and sample the node's state for a bounded window: the control should reach Leader, the flagged case should stay Follower.

latest_interpretation.rationale: Receipt f5cb1459db5e418d9a9aa6987ef76dfc (exit 0, fourteen events, no parse loss) settles both comparisons of this question. Comparison 0 is violated by witness event index 11: after restarting the single-voter node with RestoreCommittedLogs on and no snapshot, became_leader is false and the final state is Follower across the whole 1500 ms sampling window, with after_latest_index 0 and the matching admission event recording before_latest_index 1 with one server. Comparison 1 holds at evaluated event index 13: the identical restart without the flag reported became_leader true, final state Leader and after_latest_index 1, so the difference tracks the recovery flag rather than restart timing. Source: with an empty latest configuration runFollower takes the 'no known peers, aborting election' branch and never sets Candidate (raft.go:228-232); even on the candidate path quorumSize() would be one while electSelf asks only the servers in that same empty list (raft.go:1087-1094, 1999-2060); and the configuration is empty because restoreFromCommittedLogs advanced lastApplied past the committed LogConfiguration before the startup scan (api.go:604-620, 724-754). Consequence under the witnessed conditions: a single-voter cluster that restarts with this flag never regains a leader, so duties needing a leader stay pending with no enabled path to completion, since the node's own committed log holds the configuration it would need. The multi-voter variant of the same question was later witnessed under the child question: with a five-voter committed configuration a restarted node kept the stale three-voter configuration and won leadership on two of the committed five votes (receipt abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407, violated at witness event index 22, control holding at 25), so the authority loss is not confined to an empty configuration.
counterevidence: The flag-off control reaches Leader inside the same 1500 ms window, so the non-campaigning is not a general restart delay.

The library deliberately grants votes when the server list is empty (a bootstrap affordance), which explains why such a node still answers vote requests; the witnessed defect is the state it resumes with, not the vote-granting rule.
limitations: This question's own witness is a single-voter configuration with no snapshot; the stale multi-voter election is witnessed under the child question and cited there, not re-observed here.
The window is bounded at 1500 ms against a 50 ms election timeout, so a much later recovery is not excluded.
The snapshot-age configuration variant is witnessed through the configuration observation and the child's election, not through this authority sample.
latest_interpretation.joint_history: Receipt f5cb1459db5e418d9a9aa6987ef76dfc is this question's own execution (single-voter node, no snapshot, wall-clock sampling of the restarted node). Receipt abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407 belongs to the child multi-voter question and is cited here only for the follow-on statement that the authority loss also occurs with a stale non-empty configuration. The two are complete executions of different scenarios rather than fragments of one history, and neither is used to establish the other's comparison.

investigations.question: Does the configuration loss also occur for a real membership change in a multi-voter cluster, and can the resulting stale membership produce a decision the committed configuration would not allow?
investigations.hypothesis: A node restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the snapshot's configuration when committed membership changes sit below the restored commit index, so its quorum arithmetic reflects an obsolete membership and it can win an election its committed configuration would forbid.
investigations.discriminator: Grow a snapshot-age three-voter cluster to five voters, restart the leader, compare the configuration index and server count with the log's latest configuration, then isolate the restarted node with one committed voter and check whether it wins with the smaller quorum while the majority side keeps a leader.

Configuration: receipt b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826, violated at witness event index 15 - the node restarted from a log whose latest configuration is index 14 with five servers came back at configuration index 1 with three servers - control holding at index 18. Election: abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407, violated at witness index 22 - the isolated node became leader with reachable_votes 2 against committed_quorum 3 - control holding at index 25. Acknowledgements: 568bebb18e574cafa18e96add68e89db, violated at witness index 27 (the isolated leader's Apply completed), and f0db8b71047e42df96d3e2f4f581835c, violated at witness index 27 (both sides acknowledged a client write concurrently), each with its control holding at index 29. Log agreement after healing: a608e5f60ae4415981c1024522a24a0d and its repeat 6fc5c2c2f19c47a18d9613a11dd9863f, both violated at witness event index 27 - eight seconds after healing the two nodes hold different entries at the same log index while both_sides_acknowledged is true and neither node applied an entry absent from its own log - controls holding at index 29. Source: restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) advances lastApplied to the persisted commit index before the startup scan at api.go:604-620, so AddVoter's later entry (api.go:994-1005) is never re-read and the node keeps the snapshot's three-server list; quorumSize() (raft.go:1087-1094) then returns two, electSelf (raft.go:1999-2060) asks only that list, and commitment accepts two matching indexes, so leadership and acknowledgements rest on a majority of an obsolete configuration while the two sides never reconcile across the index they each wrote.

knowledge.statement: At startup the in-memory configuration (r.configurations.latest/committed) is produced only by restoreSnapshot (the latest snapshot's configuration) and by the NewRaft log scan over indexes greater than max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied). With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, restoreFromCommittedLogs sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index before that scan, so a committed LogConfiguration entry at an index <= the restored commit index is never processed and the node keeps the snapshot configuration, or an empty configuration when no snapshot exists.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; the persisted commit index from GetCommitIndex is at least the index of the latest committed LogConfiguration entry; no snapshot covers that entry (no snapshot at all, or snapshot.ConfigurationIndex below it).

knowledge.statement: With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and no snapshot, NewRaft replays the committed log by pushing one fsmMutateCh message per MaxAppendEntries-sized batch before the FSM goroutine is started; when the committed backlog requires more batches than the queue's 128 slots, the send blocks and NewRaft never returns, so the node never starts.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore, no snapshot covering the committed range, and a restored commit index whose replay needs more than 128 batches of MaxAppendEntries entries (DefaultConfig sets MaxAppendEntries 64 and TrailingLogs 10240, so about 8192 retained entries; MaxAppendEntries is validated positive and at most 1024, so the boundary scales with the configured value); observed for 8402 entries (132 batches) with a bounded 15 second wait, against 8002 entries (126 batches) returning in 0-3 ms.

knowledge.statement: A node restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs whose rebuilt configuration is empty stays a Follower and never campaigns: the latest configuration is empty, so runFollower takes the 'no known peers, aborting election' branch and quorumSize() returns one, while the same node restarted without the flag rebuilds the committed configuration and returns to Leader.
knowledge.conditions: Single-voter configuration bootstrapped in the log, Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with CommitTrackingLogStore, no snapshot so the startup configuration scan starts above the committed configuration entry; observed over a 1500 ms window with a 50 ms election timeout.

knowledge.statement: A node restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs whose latest snapshot predates committed membership changes resumes with the snapshot's configuration: after growing a three-voter cluster to five voters, the restarted leader held configuration index 1 with three servers while its own log's latest configuration was index 14 with five servers, and the same restart without the flag kept index 14 with five servers.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; one snapshot taken before the membership change (automatic snapshots disabled); the committed configuration entry's index at or below the persisted commit index restored by restoreFromCommittedLogs.

knowledge.statement: A node restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs whose rebuilt configuration is a stale, smaller membership can be elected leader with support that is a minority of the committed configuration: isolated together with one committed voter it became leader with two votes while the committed five-voter configuration requires three, and the same restart without the flag could not win on that side.
knowledge.conditions: Committed configuration grown from three to five voters after the node's snapshot; RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; the restarted node isolated together with one committed voter immediately after NewRaft returns, with that partner also cut off from the majority side so requestVote's existing-leader guard does not refuse it; observed with a bounded window against a flag-off control.

knowledge.statement: A node restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs that keeps a stale, smaller configuration can acknowledge a client write while its support is a minority of the committed configuration: isolated together with one committed voter it became leader and its Apply completed, whereas the same restart without the flag produced no leader on that side and no acknowledgement.
knowledge.conditions: Committed configuration grown from three to five voters after the restarting node's snapshot; RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; the node isolated together with one committed voter immediately after NewRaft returns, that partner also cut off from the majority side; two second apply timeout, bounded observation window, flag-off control in the same execution.

knowledge.statement: With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, a restarted node that keeps a stale smaller configuration can both win leadership on a minority of the committed configuration and acknowledge client writes concurrently with the majority side's own leader: in one execution both sides acknowledged a client write while partitioned, and the flag-off control acknowledged only on the majority side.
knowledge.conditions: Committed configuration grown from three to five voters after the restarting node's snapshot; RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; the node isolated together with one committed voter immediately after NewRaft returns, that partner also cut off from the majority side; a bounded wait for the majority side to hold its own leader before either write; two second apply timeout and two second heal settle.

knowledge.statement: In this scenario and window no acknowledged entry was lost after healing: two seconds after the partition healed, the isolated node and the majority-side leader each still held their own acknowledged entry in their own log store, neither had applied an entry absent from its own log, and the flag-off control's isolated side never acknowledged an entry.
knowledge.conditions: Five-voter committed configuration with a three-voter snapshot; RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; the restarted node isolated with one committed voter immediately after NewRaft returns and both sides acknowledging a distinct client write; two second apply timeout and two second heal settle; in-memory log stores.
